paper.title: llama.cpp b12811
paper.abstract: ui: share conversations to Hugging Face datasets as agent traces ( #32608 ) ui: add @ggml-org/llama-huggingface, a Hugging Face account as a package A package in ui/lib that gives an app running in the browser, with no server of its own, a Hugging Face account. Its plain entry holds "Sign in with Hugging Face" (OAuth with PKCE and dynamic client registration) and the Hub calls: who the account is, its datasets, and committing a trace file to one. Its Svelte entry holds the account as state (HfAccount) and the components that show it, built on Llama UI: the account panel and the dialog that shares a trace. It knows no app: the app says who it is and hands over what to share. Llama Chat compiles it from source, like the other packages, so the llama-server image builds (.devops) and the asset staging (scripts/ui-assets.cmake) copy its sources next to the other packages'. CI checks and tests it. Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium) ui: share conversations to Hugging Face datasets as agent traces A conversation's menu and each message get a Share action. It uploads the conversation, or the branch up to that message, to a Hugging Face dataset as a JSONL trace, which the Hub shows in its trace viewer. The sign-in is part of the share: the dialog (@ggml-org/llama-huggingface) asks for it with "Sign in with Hugging Face" (contribute-repos: the app creates datasets and writes only to the ones it created) or with a pasted access token. It then shows the datasets the account can add to as tiles, with a tile to create a new one (public unless the private option is ticked); with none to add to, it asks for the name of a new dataset. A pasted token reaches every dataset of the account; a sign-in reaches the ones this browser shared to. Once shared, the dialog shows the trace as a file with the first messages of the conversation fading out below it, and every action in one place at the bottom right. Once signed in, Settings > General shows the account with its Sign out; before that it shows nothing. The builds we release have the sharing: the prebuilt UI llama-server downloads, the llama-server images and the npm package. A build of your own has it only when asked for. VITE_PUBLIC_HUGGING_FACE=true bundles the package's sign-in, upload and dialogs; without it the package's Svelte entry resolves to an inert stand-in, which CI checks against the bundle built with it. The dev server, the tests and Storybook have it. -DLLAMA_UI_HUGGING_FACE=ON adds it to llama-server's UI built from source (it builds again when the option changes), and the Docker images take the variable as a build argument. The conversation menu is now one component, ConversationActions, used by the sidebar row, the search results and the chat tabs, so each offers the same actions. Llama Chat and its llama-chat alias go to 0.4.0. paper.title: llama.cpp b12807
paper.abstract: ggml-openvino: CI op-test fixes and NPU improvements ( #33088 ) ggml-openvino: KV-only prefill on the static path, with one decode step for the outputs On the static path (NPU, or any device with GGML_OPENVINO_FORCE_STATIC=1) the prefill model of a graph with KV-shared attention layers is compiled with only the cache writes as outputs. The new conversion pass KeepCacheResults (openvino/pass/keep_cache_results.cpp, registered in pass_registry/common.cpp from GraphTraits::kv_only_outputs) removes the other Results and the Parameters nothing reads any more, so OpenVINO drops everything that only feeds the logits: for models whose tail layers read an earlier layer's KV (Gemma 3n/4 E-series) every KV-shared layer and the LM head. When the batch needs logits, the decode model is run once on the output token: it rewrites that token's KV rows with the same values and runs the dropped layers against the complete cache. The decoder keeps its full output list and only reports which outputs are caches; an imported cached model takes the cache outputs as its output names. It is on by default and applies only where it pays off and is valid: graphs with KV-shared attention, at most one output token per batch, and no HFA prefill or decode KV windows. GGML_OPENVINO_KV_ONLY_PREFILL=0 turns it off; the earlier name GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_KV_ONLY_PREFILL is still accepted. Gemma 4 E2B Q4_0 on NPU (KV_SLICE=0, NPU_TURBO=YES): llama-bench pp512 1320-1375 -> 2349-2454 t/s, pp2048 1146-1202 -> 2268-2513 t/s; E4B pp512 587 -> 773, pp2048 591 -> 847 t/s. llama-server, E2B, 3016-token prompt, prefill chunk 512, context checkpoints off: 1097-1108 -> 2136-2448 t/s. Greedy outputs match the full prefill on 3 of 4 needle prompts; the fourth differs by one near-tie token that also flips between baseline runs. ggml-openvino: NPU host gather for large embedding tables GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_HOST_GATHER=1 gathers the rows of large host-resident embedding tables (at least 64 MiB, raw GGUF data, ids from a graph input) on the host. The static graph gets the rows through a ggml_host_rows_ input instead of an OpenVINO Gather over the table. With NPUW function calls the table becomes a function input, and gathering from an input that large costs about as much as streaming the whole table every call: 21.6 ms of the ~62 ms Gemma 4 E2B decode step, against 0.45 ms for the same partition with the table baked in. A table used only for such lookups (the Gemma 3n/4 per-layer embedding table) is no longer converted, requantized or bound to the NPU. Gemma 4 on NPU (NPU_TURBO=YES, KV_SLICE=0, 868-token prompt), together with KV-only prefill: E2B decode 65.3 -> 40.3 ms/token, prefill 925 -> 392 ms, system commit 8.5 -> 4.4 GB, load 109 -> 61 s; E4B decode 150 -> 72 ms/token, prefill 1931 -> 1022 ms, commit 14.6 -> 9.1 GB. Greedy outputs match the default on 3 of 4 needle prompts; the fourth differs by one near-tie token that also flips between baseline runs. ggml-openvino: NPU host gather and KV-only prefill with the weightless blob cache Make the two NPU options work with GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_WEIGHTLESS_BANK / SELF_CONTAINED_MMAP: host gather also accepts tables in OpenVINO buffers when a raw-weight cache mode keeps (or, with SELF_CONTAINED_MMAP, wraps) the raw GGUF bytes there; a warm import binds only the decoder inputs present in the compiled blob, since KV-only prefill (out_ids) and host gather (token ids) can leave inputs unused, as HFA prefill already did; a weights file that cannot be written (e.g. a full disk) no longer fails the graph: the pair is compiled and run without being cached. Gemma 4 on NPU (NPU_TURBO=YES, KV_SLICE=0, 868-token prompt), weightless cache + MMAP warm start with host gather and KV-only prefill: E2B load 1.8 s, system commit 2.5 GB, prefill 385-414 ms, decode 39.5-41 ms/token, cache 1.5 GB; E4B load 3.3-3.6 s, commit 4.7-4.8 GB, prefill ~1.0 s, decode 68.5-69.8 ms/token, cache 3.3 GB. Greedy outputs are byte-identical to the default path on export and import. ggml-openvino: let GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_TOKEN_EMBD_QUANT apply to Q4_K/Q5_K tables when set Q4_K and Q5_K token_embd tables default to the channel-wise int8 of ggml_openvino_get_requant_type() on NPU and ignored GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_TOKEN_EMBD_QUANT. They now follow it when it is set explicitly; the Q6_K behaviour and all defaults are unchanged. Gemma 4 E2B ties a Q4_K table to the output layer: int8 stores it in 384 MiB, q4_0_128 in 198 MiB (llama-server working set -0.18 GB; accuracy not yet measured). ggml-openvino: export prefill model of every KV window for weightless bank cache With a weightless-bank model cache and sliced (non head-major) KV, round the static prefill attention size up to the decode KV window, so prefill sizes are the window sizes (1024/2048/4096/8192). The export run (SELF_CONTAINED_MMAP=0) then builds the prefill model of every window at startup, so an import-only run (SELF_CONTAINED_MMAP=1) has a pair for any prompt length. ggml-openvino: integer KV_SLICE, KV-only with decode windows, gemma-4 pruned masks GGML_OPENVINO_KV_SLICE takes 0, 1 or a multiple of 256 as the base of the attended KV windows; decode windows (BLOB_PREBUILD) use the same base. KV-only prefill works together with decode KV windows: the output step runs the decode model of the window the next decode step uses. gemma-4 prune_shared (upstream #32342 ) adds host-filled out_mask/out_mask_swa and inp_prune_ids/inp_prune_keep inputs. The pruned masks are not graph inputs: their rows are gathered in the OV model from the (sliced, padded) input masks with inp_prune_ids. The KV-only output step ignores inp_prune_keep, and HFA prefill is not used for the pruned masks. ggml-openvino: keep the compiled model alive while reading its inputs (-Wdangling-reference) ggml-openvino: make the NPU weightless-bank cache automatic with the model cache dir Remove GGML_OPENVINO_SELF_CONTAINED_BLOB, GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_WEIGHTLESS_BANK and GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_SHARED_BANK. On NPU, setting GGML_OPENVINO_COMPILED_MODEL_CACHE_DIR alone now selects the weightless-bank cache layout. Why The self-contained (SC) mode embedded the full weights into every exported blob and kept separate ggml-sc-prefill / ggml-sc-decode NPUW banks. Compared to the weightless bank (WB) it: wrote the weights once per blob (prefill, decode and every KV window), so the cache was several times larger; disabled the decode KV windows (decode_bucket returned 0), so decode always ran at the full context; needed an in-process keep-alive workaround; was much slower and heavier to import. Earlier phi-4-mini data: SC import 38 s / 8.8 GB InUse / 636 prefill t/s vs WB 3.7 s / 3.3 GB / 1245 t/s. WB was strictly better, so it becomes the only NPU cache layout and the three opt-in switches are dropped. New behaviour If the directory holds valid blobs, manifests and the shared weights file for the prefill/decode pair, they are imported directly ("model cache HIT (weightless bank)"). Otherwise the models are compiled and exported as weightless blobs plus one <weights_fp>-<weights_fp>.weights.bin shared by every prefill/decode pair and KV window, and a warning is logged ("no usable cached blob(s) in ...; compiling and exporting ... as weightless-bank blobs"). The same warning is logged for each decode KV window and each prefill KV window that has to be compiled. NPU graphs without a KV cache no longer use the model cache and always compile. GGML_OPENVINO_SELF_CONTAINED_MMAP is kept (GGUF mmap as weight buffer, lazy large compute buffers). It now needs only NPU + cache dir, stays import-only and its error messages name the cache directory. The fingerprint tag of weightless blobs is unchanged, so existing weightless caches (exported with NPU_WEIGHTLESS_BANK=1) remain valid. Code changes ggml-openvino-extra.{h,cpp}: drop the SELF_CONTAINED_BLOB, NPU_WEIGHTLESS_BANK and NPU_SHARED_BANK entries from the env table; replace ggml_openvino_npu_raw_weight_cache_enabled() and ggml_openvino_npu_weightless_bank_enabled() with ggml_openvino_npu_weightless_cache_enabled() (NPU && cache dir set); drop the SELF_CONTAINED_BLOB early return in ggml_openvino_npu_decode_bucket(). ggml-openvino.cpp: raw weight upload, keeping the raw weights on Windows and the self-contained mmap buffer now key off the new helper. ggml-decoder.cpp: the raw-cache checks, including is_host_gather_rows(), use the new helper. utils.{h,cpp}: drop the embedded-weight (self-contained) blob path, the in-process keep-alive and the shared-bank sc-prefill/sc-decode branch; remove the self_contained field from static_build_args and ov_compiled_graph. model_cache_dir is left empty for NPU graphs without a KV cache; weightless_bank = NPU && cache dir set. Import with skipped weights always uses ov::weights_path + enable_weightless; compile enables weightless export whenever the weightless bank is in use. model-cache.h: comments updated for the single cache layout. Docs: OPENVINO.md and OpenVINO-ENV-VARS.md drop the removed variables and describe the automatic weightless bank. Port notes Cherry-picked from d97d7fb (refact-cache-v0) onto xuejun/gemma4-e2b-v1. Conflicts in ggml-openvino-extra.cpp, utils.h and utils.cpp were resolved by keeping this branch's newer features and only removing SC/WB/SHARED: GGML_OPENVINO_KV_ONLY_PREFILL and GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_HOST_GATHER (env entries and helpers) are kept; ggml_openvino_npu_decode_bucket() keeps this branch's "BLOB_PREBUILD ? ggml_openvino_kv_slice_base() : 0"; ov_compiled_graph keeps prefill_fp / decode_fp; a leftover ggml_openvino_npu_raw_weight_cache_enabled() call in ggml-decoder.cpp (from a branch-only commit) was switched to the new helper. Verification phi-4-mini Q4_0 llama-server on NPU (c=8192, chunk 1024, KV_SLICE=1, BLOB_PREBUILD=1, LAZY_HOST_THRESHOLD_MB=128, no bank env var set): cold export: weightless bank selected automatically, 8 blobs (prefill + decode for KV windows 1024/2048/4096/8192, 3.6-10.8 MB each) + one 2125 MB weights.bin; load 67.3 s, prefill 1119 t/s, decode 22.09 t/s; 3 imports with SELF_CONTAINED_MMAP=1, all blobs cache HIT, no recompile: avg of 3 imports baseline(lazy128) this commit delta LoadMs 3822 3686 -3.6% InUseDeltaMB 3398 3470 +2.1% Prefill t/s 1260 1253 -0.6% Decode t/s 22.45 22.67 +1.0% compare_baseline.ps1 -Variant lazy128: within tolerance. llama-simple smoke test on NPU passes. ggml-openvino: remove GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_PARALLEL_COMPILE Drop the opt-in switch that compiled the NPU prefill and decode models concurrently. Prefill and decode are now always compiled one after the other, which was already the default behaviour. Why It was off by default and not used by any preset, launch config or bench script. It only applied when the weightless bank was off. Since the weightless bank is now automatic whenever GGML_OPENVINO_COMPILED_MODEL_CACHE_DIR is set on NPU, it could only take effect for uncached runs. Compiling both models at the same time raises the host memory peak during load, which works against the memory-reduction work on NPU. It added a second, rarely tested code path around build_static_model(). Code changes ggml-openvino-extra.{h,cpp}: remove the GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_PARALLEL_COMPILE env table entry and ggml_openvino_npu_parallel_compile_enabled(). utils.cpp: remove the parallel_compile flag and the std::async branch in the static (NPU) compile path; keep the sequential prefill -> decode compile, including the no-KV-cache and shared decode_source cases, unchanged. Update the comments that mentioned parallel compilation and drop the now unused include. dev_doc/OpenVINO-ENV-VARS.md: remove the variable from the table. A leftover GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_PARALLEL_COMPILE in the environment is now reported as an unknown variable and ignored. Verification llama-server and llama-simple build with GGML_OPENVINO (MSVC Release). llama-simple granite-4.0-1b Q4_0 on NPU decodes 20 tokens correctly. ggml-openvino: apply clang-format docs : add a gemma-4 E2B NPU example with the model cache docs : update docs ggml-openvino: remove dead code and simplify env handling ggml-openvino: add GGML_OPENVINO_DEBUG_DYNAMIC_DIMS ggml-openvino: one compiled-model cache per static (NPU) graph Replace the static-path cache bookkeeping with a single cache per cgraph entry. The key is the cgraph; the value is a map of compiled models, one per static variant (prefill/decode, KV window, SWA window, output length), each holding its own infer request. Why The static (NPU) path kept compiled models in several places that had to be kept in sync: a prefill/decode "compiled pair" in ov_compiled_graph shared across backends through compiled_cache->graphs; per-KV-window decode and prefill models plus their requests and I/O name caches in ov_runtime_context; a process-wide table of imported blobs (g_imported_blobs / import_cached_blob / ov_clear_imported_blobs). Export, import, KV-window switching and fallback each walked a different subset of these, which made the logic hard to follow and to change. New structure utils.h: ov_static_variant_key {prefill, attention_size, attention_size_swa, output_len}, ordered and comparable. ov_static_variant {compiled model, lazily created infer request, input/output names}. decoder_runtime_ctx owns std::map<key, variant> variants plus the per-graph state shared by all variants (kv_only_prefill, decode_unfold, cache_base_extra, prefill/decode prepared flags and the weights path/bank/layout). ov_compiled_graph is reduced to the fields used by the dynamic path; the prefill request/name caches are removed from ov_runtime_context. utils.cpp (static path): Small helpers before ov_graph_compute_static: variant key list, fingerprint, weights selection, blob usability check, decoder build, compile config, conversion, weights layout and static_load_variants(). static_load_variants() imports every usable blob and compiles the rest in one place. The first prefill and decode models are still converted before any compile (Bonsai-8B ordering). Each model logs "<prefill|decode> model of KV window N imported/compiled in X ms". ov_graph_compute_static() now: looks up the entry, resets it when the graph cannot be reused, picks the needed prefill key and the decode key, loads what is missing, then takes the request from the variant (created on first use). The KV-only output step and KV growth use the same variant map; the separate decode-window request switching is gone. Removed g_imported_blobs, import_cached_blob() and ov_clear_imported_blobs(). ggml-openvino.cpp: drop the ov_clear_imported_blobs() call in backend free. model-cache.cpp is unchanged. Cache behaviour (GGML_OPENVINO_COMPILED_MODEL_CACHE_DIR set on NPU) GGML_OPENVINO_SELF_CONTAINED_MMAP=0: models with a usable blob are imported, all missing ones (every prefill/decode KV window) are compiled and exported as weightless-bank blobs plus the shared weights file. GGML_OPENVINO_SELF_CONTAINED_MMAP=1: every model is imported from the cache. A missing blob now fails immediately with "GGML_OPENVINO_SELF_CONTAINED_MMAP: no usable cached <prefill|decode> model of KV window N in ; run once with GGML_OPENVINO_SELF_CONTAINED_MMAP=0 to build the cache". Compiling after the host weights were released still fails fast. The fingerprint formula (cache_base_extra and per-variant salt) is unchanged, so existing caches stay valid: a fresh phi-4-mini export produces the same 8 blob names as a cache from the previous commit. Behaviour changes Compiled models belong to their backend entry and are no longer shared across backends through compiled_cache->graphs. Without head-major KV, an export compiles all prefill KV windows but keeps only the needed one resident; the others are imported from the cache on first use. With SELF_CONTAINED_MMAP=1 or head-major KV all variants are kept.
